h1: Exterior Painting in Archer, FL for Homes in Full Sun
heroIntro: Archer homes often sit in open ground with no tree line to soften the sun or rain. Our exterior system is built for that exposure, from the wash to the final coat.

sections.h2: What open ground does to an Archer exterior
body: Drive the back roads around Archer and you will see the pattern: farmhouses and ranch homes with nothing between them and the sky. That exposure is beautiful, and hard on paint. With no neighboring houses or trees for cover, the south and west elevations take hours of direct afternoon sun, so they chalk, fade, and crack first. Summer storms throw rain sideways across open fields, and the bottom courses of siding pick up sandy splashback.

Meanwhile the shaded spots, like porch ceilings, the north wall, and anywhere sprinklers hit, stay damp and grow mildew. A good exterior painting job in Archer, FL has to handle both extremes on the same house.

sections.h2: The exterior system, step by step
bullets: Wash and treat mildew at the root so nothing grows under the new film
Scrape loose paint to a sound edge and sand gloss for adhesion
Take moisture readings on suspect wood; replace rotted fascia and trim
Set nail pops and re-caulk moving joints with flexible sealant
Spot-prime bare wood and tannin-bleeding boards
Two full coats of 100% acrylic on siding and trim; elastomeric where stucco has hairline cracks
Back-brush or back-roll sprayed surfaces where penetration matters
body: Glass, hardware, fixtures, plantings, and drives are masked before spraying. Landscaping is rinsed at the end of the day.

Doors and shutters get the same attention as the siding. Front doors facing west take a beating, and a harder enamel finish keeps them looking sharp longer; see door and shutter painting for the details.

sections.h2: Timing the work around Archer weather
body: October through May is the sweet spot for exterior painting here: lower humidity, cooler surfaces, and fewer afternoon storms. Summer work is still possible, but we start earlier in the day, track dew point, and watch radar so coatings are not rained on before they set. A full exterior generally takes three to seven working days, plus washing and dry time. More on how weather affects coatings is in our guide to Florida painting weather.

Archer exteriors carry a written workmanship warranty of up to 10 years, on top of the manufacturer's product warranty. Anything not right at the final walkthrough is fixed before the job closes, and labelled touch-up paint stays with you. If the siding is just dirty rather than failing, a soft wash in Archer may buy you more time before a repaint. Planning the whole house? See residential painting in Archer.

faqs.q: Why is my west wall peeling when the north side looks fine?
faqs.a: Afternoon sun heats and breaks down the film on west and south walls much faster. We often see chalking and cracking there years before other sides, especially on open Archer lots.

faqs.q: Can you paint in summer in Archer?
faqs.a: Yes, but we work earlier in the day and watch dew point and radar. October through May is the best window for exterior projects.

faqs.q: Do you paint fiber-cement and wood siding differently?
faqs.a: Both get 100% acrylic, but bare or weathered wood is spot-primed first and checked for rot. The product line for each surface is named on your estimate.

faqs.q: What does the exterior warranty cover?
faqs.a: Workmanship, in writing, for up to 10 years on exterior projects, in addition to the paint manufacturer's own product warranty.
